title: Social Priors: Descriptions of AI Users Shape How Language Models Trust and Cooperate
abstract: arXiv:2610.16946v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Descriptions of how people use AI are becoming training data for the next generation of models. We ask whether what a model reads about its users changes how it treats people. Using contrastive synthetic-document finetuning, we train Qwen3-32B on four matched corpora built from the same 1,625 real-world usage scenarios. The corpora differ only in the predominant motive they attribute to users of AI chatbots: helping others (prosocial), exploiting others (antisocial), legitimate self-advancement, or task completion. Finetuning shifts the models' stated beliefs about users, how true those beliefs look along an internal truth direction, and their broader judgments of how safe and good the world is. These social priors carry into behavior. In trust games, antisocial models expect less reciprocity and send less money than prosocial models. translated_title: 社会先验：对AI用户的描述如何塑造语言模型的信任与合作行为
translated_abstract: 关于人们如何使用AI的描述正在成为下一代模型的训练数据。我们探究模型所读到的关于其用户的内容是否会改变它对待人的方式。通过对比性合成文档微调方法，我们基于相同的1,625个真实使用场景构建了四个匹配的语料库来训练Qwen3-32B模型。这些语料库仅在赋予AI聊天机器人用户的主要动机上有所不同：帮助他人（亲社会）、利用他人（反社会）、正当的自我提升，或任务完成。微调改变了模型对用户的明确信念、这些信念沿内部真值方向所呈现的真实程度，以及模型对世界安全与美好程度的更广泛判断。这些社会先验会延续到行为层面：在信任博弈中，反社会模型比亲社会模型预期更少的互惠行为，并汇出更少的金额。它们的不信任是具体且针对人的，尤其是针对AI聊天机器人的用户。
tldr: 该研究通过对比性合成文档微调发现，训练数据中对AI用户动机的描述（亲社会或反社会）会在语言模型中形成“社会先验”，不仅改变模型对用户的信念，还会实际影响其在信任博弈中表现出的信任与合作行为。
en_tdlr: Training data that describes AI users' motives creates "social priors" in language models—fine-tuning Qwen3-32B on corpora framing users as prosocial versus antisocial shifts both the models' stated beliefs about users and their actual trust and cooperation behavior in trust games.
